span.label: scale-free network - the term in general use, which the review says applies only to the degree distribution and not to the network's other properties
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: network - the stipulated vocabulary of the review: a set of items called vertices, with connections between them called edges
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `connectivity` - A NAME THIS REVIEW REFUSES, AND IT SAYS WHY: `Quotation withheld` A refusal grounded in COLLISION WITH A NEIGHBOURING FIELD rather than in the term being wrong - the new usage is intelligible and is declined because the word is already taken.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `network density` - THE SAME WORDS NAMING A DIFFERENT QUANTITY BY FIELD: in sociology it names the LOCAL clustering coefficient Ci of a single vertex, which is what this passage records. Elsewhere `density` names the global edge count over possible edges. A reader who imports the sociological sense into the physics literature is reading a per-vertex quantity as a whole-graph one.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `assortative mixing` / `homophily` / `assortative matching` - ONE PHENOMENON, THREE NAMES, AND THE REVIEW ATTRIBUTES EACH TO ITS FIELD: `called ASSORTATIVE MIXING OR HOMOPHILY` in social networks and epidemiology, while `the term ASSORTATIVE MATCHING is also seen in THE ECOLOGY LITERATURE, particularly in reference to mate choice among animals`. The ecological name carries a narrower referent - mate choice - inside the same concept.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `clustering coefficient` / `fraction of transitive triples` - ONE QUANTITY, TWO FIELD-LOCAL NAMES, and the review is explicit that the DEFINITION is the same one: `The definition of C GIVEN HERE has been widely used in the sociology literature, WHERE IT IS REFERRED TO AS the “fraction of transitive triples”.` FILED AS A SENSE AND NOT AS A `renamed-across-fields` EDGE ON PURPOSE: the gate requires a renaming clause to contain BOTH names, and this one calls the physics-side quantity `C` rather than `clustering coefficient`. The only span naming both runs back through Eq. (3). A CLAUSE NAMING ONE NAME IS A DEFINITION, NOT A RENAMING - the gate is right, and the reading survives at the sense layer where it is grounded in what the sentence actually says.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `Vertex` / `site` / `node` / `actor` - ONE OBJECT, FOUR NAMES, AND THE PAPER PRINTS THE DISCIPLINE BESIDE EACH. `The fundamental unit of a network, ALSO CALLED A SITE (PHYSICS), A NODE (COMPUTER SCIENCE), OR AN ACTOR (SOCIOLOGY).` **This is the corpus's cleanest instance of renaming-across-fields**: not reconstructed from two papers that never cite each other, but asserted in a glossary by an author who works in all three literatures. The same sentence does it AGAIN for `Edge` / `bond` / `link` / `tie`, with the same three fields in the same order.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `clustering` - A NAME THAT COLLIDES INSIDE ITS OWN FIELD, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO WHILE USING IT. `Quotation withheld` The other meaning is community detection. **The alias is not across fields - it is a collision WITHIN one**, and the author records the ambiguity rather than resolving it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: qualifies → Barabási and Albert, preferential attachment
span.note: differs in: WHICH NAME THE MODEL TRAVELS UNDER, AND THE REVIEW SAYS THE EARLIER ONE DID NOT: 'The work of PRICE himself, however, is LARGELY UNKNOWN in the scientific community, and CUMULATIVE ADVANTAGE did not achieve currency as a model of network growth until its REDISCOVERY some decades later by Barabási and Albert, Quotation withheld.' One mechanism, two names, and the currency followed the second - so a search on either name finds only half the literature
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the preferential-attachment model as a model of the Web
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE MODEL'S OWN PREDICTION APPEARS IN THE DATA IT IS APPLIED TO. The model implies older vertices have higher degree; 'This correlation between degree and age has been used by Adamic and Huberman to ARGUE AGAINST THE MODEL as a model of the World Wide Web - Quotation withheld.' The refutation is of the model AS APPLIED TO THE WEB, not of the mechanism in general
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reinterprets → Milgram's small-world experiment
span.note: differs in: WHAT THE SAME EXPERIMENT IS EVIDENCE FOR. 'there is ANOTHER CONCLUSION that can be drawn from this experiment WHICH MILGRAM APPARENTLY FAILED TO NOTICE; it was pointed out in 2000 by Kleinberg' - roughly three decades later. The finding was in the data the whole time and needed a different question asked of it, which is the strongest kind of case for a layer that records what a result was taken to show
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A review synthesizing complex-network science across social, information, technological, and biological networks: unifying concepts include the small-world effect, degree distributions (scale-free power laws), clustering, random-graph and preferential-attachment growth models, and dynamical processes on networks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same structural properties recur across otherwise unrelated systems (Internet, social, biological networks) — a common science of networks.
